  • Zero Open source
    An open-source terminal coding agent written in Go that works with 30+ model providers, supports MCP, skills and subagents, and keeps all sessions on your own disk.
  • AOCI-CODE Open source
    AOCI-CODE keeps a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that your coding agent writes and a local MCP server governs. Agents in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode read the map once and know what each file is for, what it depends on and what must not break, instead of re-reading the repo on every task. It can index an existing codebase of up to about half a million lines and report how well it knows each area before taking over development.
  • Waku Open source
    Waku is a native desktop app that gathers your local coding agents in one place. It shows sessions from Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Pi on a single timeline that stays entirely on your machine, so you can follow and switch between agent runs without juggling terminals.
  • Kodus Open source + cloud
    Self-hostable AI code reviewer for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps pull requests that works with the model you choose.
  • Wake Free and open source (MIT); macOS 14+, Linux and Windows beta
    Wake is a desktop app that collects every coding-agent conversation on your computer into one searchable place. It reads the local history kept by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Devin and other agents, groups sessions by agent and project, and lets you find a past conversation in seconds and resume it in your terminal. It is read-only and nothing leaves your machine. Built in Rust, it runs on macOS, with Linux and Windows in beta.
  • Paritok Open source + cloud
    Paritok is a compression gateway that sits between a coding agent and its LLM. Using its own open-source 4B code-aware model, it shrinks tool output, files and conversation history on the fly without losing what the agent needs, which cuts token bills and lets agent sessions run longer before they hit context limits.
  • CLI Agent Orchestrator Open source
    AWS Labs tool that coordinates several coding CLIs such as Claude Code, Kiro and Codex as a team, each in its own tmux session.
  • Lody Open source + cloud
    A team workspace for running AI coding agents in parallel in isolated Git worktrees, with live diff review, GitHub integration and access from phone or desktop.
  • OpenHarness Open source
    OpenHarness from Autonomous is a native command center for running coding agents side by side, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp and Copilot. It links your laptop, home server and GPU box into one window with a password instead of SSH keys or port forwarding, keeps code and keystrokes end-to-end encrypted through its relay, and is keyboard first. Agents keep working when you close it, and it extends beyond code to CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.
  • tty7 Open source
    A terminal workbench whose shell sessions survive closing the app, built so coding agents can drive other agents' terminals and you can reattach remotely.
  • Reticle Embeddable SDK packages are Apache-2.0; the server, init and test packages are FSL-1.1-ALv2 (free for internal use, Apache-2.0 after two years); the hosted platform at app.reticle.sh is free to start with no credit card; enterprise features need a paid licence (price not listed publicly)
    Verification layer for AI coding agents: a dev-only SDK inside your web or desktop app lets the agent drive real flows and read network calls, app state and console, then returns a pass, fail or cannot-tell verdict with the file and line to fix; saved flows replay without an AI model and can gate CI.
  • Hercules Open source
    Open-source testing agent that turns plain Gherkin steps into end-to-end UI, API, accessibility and security tests.
  • Pydantic Deep Agents Open source
    Self-hosted terminal AI assistant and Python framework on Pydantic AI, with tool calling, sandboxed execution, multi-agent teams and checkpoints.
  • luvus Open source
    Mission control for AI coding agents: run, watch, resume and orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, opencode and others from one terminal with a live view of each agent.
  • Repo Prompt Open source + cloud
    The community edition of Repo Prompt, a native macOS context-engineering app that packs the right files into prompts for AI coding work and exposes the same tools to agents via MCP.
  • ThinkRail Open source
    JetBrains' lightweight agentic IDE that pairs you with the pi coding agent, with isolated git-worktree workspaces, editor tabs, terminals and diffs.
  • hax Open source
    A minimalist terminal coding agent shipped as a single native C binary using a few MB of RAM, with first-class local models plus OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter support.
  • Cloudroom Self-hosted core free (Apache-2.0); cloud: Free $0 (100 cloud agents/month, 25 hours), Pro $50/mo, Super $150/mo, Ultra $500/mo
    Cloudroom runs Claude Code, Codex, Pi and other coding agents in the cloud, each in its own isolated sandbox on its own Git branch, using your own model logins; the Rust core is open source to self-host, and a desktop app manages local and cloud agents.
  • Next.js DevTools MCP Open source (MIT license); free to use
    Vercel's MCP server that connects coding agents to running Next.js dev servers for live errors, routes, logs and docs.
  • OpenQodex Open source
    Code review that runs inside your coding agent before you push, combining security and quality scanners with a separate AI reviewer.
  • Sno Station Sno Station is open source (Apache-2.0) with a free weekly cloud allowance; Plus $19/mo, Max $199/mo, pay-as-you-go balance from $10
    Sno Station turns the coding agents you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw) into one squad on your machine with shared memory, and its Self Learning reviews their sessions and proposes skill-file fixes you approve.
  • PiG Open source
    PiG is a faithful Go port of Pi, the open-source terminal coding agent, first developed at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. It keeps Pi's behaviour and extension model while shipping as a single fast Go binary, so you can run the same minimal, hackable coding agent without a Node.js runtime.
  • Tov Free and open source (MIT); experimental v0.0.1
    Tov is an experimental programming language designed to be written by coding agents. It uses TypeScript syntax minus a few traps (no any, null or loose equality, separate int and float types, and failing calls marked with try), so agents already know how to write it, and its compiler returns machine-readable fixes the agent can apply after every edit. Programs compile to small, fast native binaries, with published benchmarks against Rust, Bun and Node. Agents can learn it from the site's llms.txt.
  • Frontman Open source
    Browser-based AI coding agent: click an element in your running app, describe the change, and it edits the source with hot reload.
  • Concord Open source + cloud
    Concord lets coding agents message each other and work together in a shared workspace. Agents running in different tools or on different machines can hand off tasks, ask each other questions and review each other's code in real time through its MCP server, so a team of agents can coordinate without you copying messages between terminals.
  • agent-manager Open source
    agent-manager is a terminal app built on tmux for running many AI coding agents at once. It shows live status for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Grok, Cursor and other sessions in a foldable project tree, adds a quick prompt bar, and has a diff reviewer whose line comments are sent straight back to the right agent, on macOS, Linux and Windows.
  • Reason Network Open source
    A small peer-to-peer daemon that links coding-agent sessions across your team's computers, so Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents can see who is working on what and message each other directly, with no server.
  • CodeAF Open source
    CodeAF is an open-source software factory from AgentField built to run on open models. It ships ready-made specialist agents you call with slash commands, one to build features like a senior developer, one to audit code for security issues and one to review GitHub pull requests, and spreads the work across a pool of models to balance cost and quality.
  • mu Open source
    mu is an open-source coding agent with a judgment kernel: a small, fast judge model makes the many routine decisions in each turn so the main model only gets the context it needs. It ships as a command-line tool and a desktop app and aims to keep coding sessions focused and cheap.
  • Foremerge Open source
    Foremerge is an open-source coordination layer for teams of coding agents, built on top of Git. Each agent keeps its own worktree, but they share what they intend to change, claim the parts of the code they are working on and verify each other's change sets, so conflicting plans are caught before they turn into merge conflicts. It also works over MCP.
  • Elephant-Goldfish Model Open source
    Elephant-Goldfish Model is an open-source method and plugin from Google for spec-driven development with AI coding agents. A deep-context agent drafts the design, then fresh zero-context subagents stress-test that spec for gaps and wrong assumptions before any code is written, which catches problems that a single long-running agent tends to miss.
  • Machinist Open source
    Machinist is an open-source software factory for coding agents. It runs agent jobs on your laptop, a virtual machine or a Kubernetes cluster, connects to GitHub so you can review the changes they make, and automates routine repository upkeep such as dependency bumps and fixes, with evals to check the results.
  • Vicoa Free $0 (1 remote machine, 10 automations); Pro $12/user/mo ($9 billed yearly); Enterprise custom; source AGPL-3.0
    Vicoa is an agent-native IDE for running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and 40+ other coding agents in parallel, each on its own git worktree, from desktop, web or phone, with notifications when an agent needs you.
  • Svelte MCP Free and open source (MIT)
    Official Svelte MCP server that gives coding agents Svelte docs and autofixing tools.
  • Muxin Free and open source (Apache-2.0)
    Muxin is a free, open-source desktop app that puts all your Macs, Linux, Windows and cloud machines in one window, so you can run Claude Code, Codex and other agent CLIs on any of them, see their screens and logs, and take changes to a pull request.
  • Shipyard Free and open source (MIT)
    Shipyard, from coss.com, runs Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents on your own dev machines, each task in its own worktree with its own terminals, dev server and live page previews, so agents keep working when your laptop sleeps.
  • Roomote Self-host free up to 10 users; Roomote Cloud from $49/mo after a 7-day trial; bring your own model key
    Cloud coding agent from the Roo Code team that runs your real dev environment, verifies its work, reviews code with a second model and hands back PRs with live previews; works from Slack, Teams, GitHub and Linear, self-hosted or on its cloud.
  • Sphinx Free and open source (MIT); questions are generated by a model you choose (your existing coding agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), so you pay only for those tokens
    Open-source Git hook for agent-assisted coding: before code your agent wrote is pushed to a protected branch, it reads the diff and quizzes you on what the change actually does when things go wrong, and only lets the push through once you answer correctly. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
  • Imbue Open source
    AI research company building tools for coding agents, including Sculptor for running parallel agents.
  • Orbi Self-hosted: free and open source (AGPL-3.0 or Sustainable Use License, bring your own model); Cloud: 3 free merged deliveries (no card), Solo $24/month (400M tokens, 1 repo), Pro $66/month (1.2B tokens, 5 repos)
    Orbi is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) software factory for GitHub repositories. When you label a GitHub Issue ai-ready, Orbi implements it in an isolated worktree, opens and reviews pull requests in a separate AI review session that checks acceptance criteria and repairs failing tests, merges the exact reviewed commit SHA, and cuts a tagged GitHub Release when a human applies the ai-release label.
  • CCC Free and source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT, free for personal and commercial use, runs locally on localhost)
    CCC (Claude Command Center) is a free, source-available local dashboard for macOS, Linux and Windows that puts every Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and five other coding-agent sessions on one visual board, highlights which session needs your input, tracks token usage and lets sessions continue on $0 models when rate limits hit.
  • Coddo Freemium
    Desktop app that puts a visual interface and voice input on top of terminal coding agents.
  • Orke Free (Microsoft Store lists it as Free); Claude Code, Codex and other AI accounts are set up separately

    AI code review that catches bugs in complex codebases on every pull request.

    Cypress's MCP server that brings Cypress Cloud test results and accessibility reports into AI coding workflows.
  • Devin Free plan; Pro $20/mo; Max $200/mo; Teams $80/mo + $40/seat

  • LayerFS Free and open source (MIT)
    LayerFS is a filesystem built for running many coding agents in parallel. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace on top of shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so compute only exists while a command runs. Every tool call becomes a commit on a branch, same-file clashes between agents are refused rather than silently merged, each line records the step that wrote it, and any commit can be forked at no cost for recursive exploration or RL training. Agents on different computers share one serverless store with chunk-level deduplication.

Extra checks can be configured for your workflow, and it is MIT licensed.

You define an agent as a TypeScript function with its model, tools and MCP servers, deploy it with one command, and every session gets its own real cloud computer, with managed sessions, schedules and API keys kept outside the agent's runtime. Templates include a coding agent that edits a repo, runs checks and opens a draft pull request, and market-research and GTM agents; its own Slack coding agent runs on it. Pricing is pay-as-you-go for model calls and per-second machine time.

  • Grok Bot Jev Router Open source (MIT); needs a TypeSafe API key (Jev is billed per input token)
    Grok Bot Jev Router is an open-source Python reference router that puts TypeSafe Jev in front of Grok Bot as a cheap decision layer. Before expensive research, browser, retry or subagent work, Jev classifies the request and returns an explicit action such as reuse a cached result, stop a failing retry, cap research, run a deterministic step, or ask a human. It starts in shadow mode that only logs decisions, has an active mode for a Grok Bot skill that honors them, and includes a kill switch. It never sends, pays or deletes anything itself.

  • Fileaify Free €0 (1 project, 5 services and secrets); Solo €4.90/month; Pro €14.90/month; Premium €39.90/month; Enterprise on request
    Fileaify is a project workspace that plugs into the coding agent you already use, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf. You give the agent one URL (fileaify.com/agent) or the hosted MCP connector, approve its access, and it finds the project's documentation, architecture decisions, roadmap and known issues in each new conversation, so you don't have to explain the project again, even when you switch agents. Credentials stay in a vault: the agent can run approved actions with them without ever seeing the keys, sensitive actions need a human's approval, and paid tiers add a sandboxed executor where the agent can actually run work. The agent also writes its contributions back into the project docs, following your review rules. A live demo project lets you try it without installing anything.

Where the TypeSafe Jev listing covers the decision model itself, this listing covers the developer API and console: send text or app context and get back a typed choice, a score or a yes/no probability for routing tools, ranking results and checking conditions, with API keys, call logs and credit use managed in one place.
  • TokenRip Free ($0/month, unlimited workspaces and agents, 1 GB storage); optional Pro $20/month (10 GB storage) and Team $50/month

  • TypeSafe Jev Usage-based: pay per input token, output free; Jev 1.14 listed at $0.042 per million input tokens in TypeSafe docs; also on OpenRouter; enterprise plans via sales
    Jev is TypeSafe's System One decision model, built for the small decisions inside software and agents. You send a state and typed questions (choice, score and more) and get typed answers with probabilities back instead of free-form text, so code can branch on them directly to route, classify, score or rank options. Agents can use it to settle narrow calls cheaply and save the larger LLM for open-ended work. Available through TypeSafe's API, Python and JavaScript SDKs, an agent skill, and OpenRouter.

    Wren x402 Doctor helps sellers of x402 pay-per-call endpoints, the payment standard AI agents use to pay for APIs in USDC, get listed in the Coinbase CDP Bazaar and stay listed. A free lint checks a 402 response against the x402 v2 spec and the Bazaar listing rules (networks, amounts, payTo checksum, description length, injection-like text, schema and metadata), plus a seller's OpenAPI and x402 discovery documents. Paid endpoints include a Bazaar health check ($0.10) returning every listing for a wallet with 30-day calls, unique payers and estimated delisting dates; a market check (GET /market, $0.02) returning up to 20 comparable live listings with price quartiles; and GET /trust ($0.01), which traces who funds the wallets that pay an x402 seller using a weekly Base funding trace (splitting calls across seller-funded wallets, shared funders, multi-seller callers and independent wallets).

  • Snyk Agent Scan Open source
    Snyk's scanner for security risks in MCP servers and agent skills.
  • Mantis Open source

  • Agent Vault Open source
    Infisical's open-source credential broker that proxies API calls for AI agents so they never hold secrets themselves.
  • open-kritt Open source + cloud
    A self-hosted AI security research tool that orchestrates agents to hunt for vulnerabilities in a codebase and then validate and rank what they find; managed scans are also offered.
  • ADR Open source
    Uber's Agentic AI Detection and Response system that secures employee and customer-facing AI agents with observability and threat detection.
  • OpenAPPA Free and open source (MIT); preview and RFC
    OpenAPPA is a deterministic guardrail that sits between an AI agent and its tools and tracks how data flows across tool calls, instead of asking a second model to judge each call. Policies decide whether untrusted or sensitive data may reach a given action, which blocks data exfiltration caused by prompt injection or hallucination while letting agents finish their tasks. It plugs into Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, kAgent and Archestra, comes with reusable policy "batteries", validation, observability and reporting, and is backed by a NeurIPS workshop paper with published benchmarks. It is in preview as an open RFC.
  • Cisco MCP Scanner Open source
    Cisco's open-source scanner that checks MCP servers and tools for malicious or risky behaviour using YARA rules and LLM analysis.
  • HOL Guard Free forever for local protection on one machine; Guard Cloud plans: Solo $4.99/mo, Pro $15/mo, Team $30/seat/mo, plus Enterprise
    HOL Guard is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0), local-first security layer for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot CLI. On supported integrations it checks risky shell commands, reads of secret-bearing files, package installs and new or changed MCP tools before they run, lets you allow, ask or block each action, and keeps a local record for review. It installs with pipx (hol-guard) and works offline; optional Guard Cloud adds synced approvals, team policy and dashboards.
  • Phase Free plan; Pro $10 per user/month; self-host free.
    An open-source secrets manager that syncs API keys and environment variables to apps, CI and agents with end-to-end encryption and access control. Free tier, Pro from $10 per user a month, or self-host.
  • Eleven Open source
    An agent-first reverse-engineering app for macOS, Windows and Linux: load any app or binary and ask your AI agent what it does while it disassembles and analyzes the code for you.
  • ThinkWatch Lite Open source
    A local gateway that sits between your coding agents and model providers, letting you switch upstreams, redact secrets before they leave your machine, block dangerous tool calls and see the cost of each request.
  • Decionis Open source + cloud
    Decionis is an approval gateway for actions taken by AI agents. It sits in front of consequential API calls such as payments, price changes and orders, checks each one against your policy before it runs, and only lets it through with a single-use permit, keeping a signed record of every decision for audit.
  • Aletheore Open source + cloud
    Aletheore audits code repositories and backs every finding with evidence. Its deterministic scanner looks for leaked secrets, vulnerable dependencies and dead code, it can watch live endpoints and draw architecture maps, and it reviews pull requests automatically through a GitHub Action. A built-in MCP server lets coding agents run the same audits.
  • 0.security Open source + cloud
    0 is an open, self-improving AI operating system for offensive security work. Its agents investigate code and binaries for vulnerabilities, test defenses, verify findings with working proofs and help fix the issues, and the team behind it publishes the advisories it has found in real open-source projects.
  • Halofy Free $0 (1 seat); Base $16/mo and Team $120/mo for 5 seats (billed yearly); Enterprise custom; governance layer AGPL-3.0
    Halofy is an access and governance layer for a team's AI agents, giving every agent organizational context through one identity and policy model with provenance and audit, alongside a desktop AI workstation that turns power users' agent practices into shared policies.
  • Speakeasy Gram Open source + cloud
    Gram is Speakeasy's open-source platform for building, hosting and governing MCP servers. Teams can turn APIs into curated MCP toolsets, host them, and manage which agents and people may use which servers from one control plane, with sign-in, access policies and usage visibility; its own MCP server lets an agent manage that setup directly.

    AI security engineer that finds vulnerabilities in applications and smart contracts and reviews pull requests; acquired by depthfirst (June 2026).
  • Is My Agent Safe Free check; full report $29 one-off; Agency $99/month founding seat (US/UK, up to 25 client installs, price locked 12 paid months)
    Is My Agent Safe explains your OpenClaw security audit and version in plain English with a red, amber or green result that puts the most important finding first and flags versions missing published security fixes; free check, full report $29 one-off, Agency seats $99/month for US and UK agencies.
  • Pragor Free public beta (3 projects, 10 agents, no card) and a permanent Free plan (1 project, 3 agents, 100 events/mo); Solo, Team and Business paid plans open after the beta
    Coordination and governance layer for teams of people and AI agents, not an autonomous agent: a shared board with tasks, directed messages, approvals, files and an attributable activity record, where agents connect over REST or project MCP access.
  • Sonatype MCP Community Edition free; Pro from $7,500/yr
    Sonatype's dependency-management MCP server that gives coding agents component versions, security analysis and Trust Score recommendations.
  • Wren Pre-sign Check Paid: $0.01 in USDC on Base per check over x402 (EIP-3009 payment authorisation, no approvals); free demo endpoints with fixed examples
    Wren Pre-sign Check is a pay-per-call x402 API that an AI agent calls before it signs anything with its wallet. Send a transaction (to + data), an EIP-712 typed-data payload or untrusted text, and it returns block, review or allow, the decoded call in plain words and every finding: unlimited approvals, Permit and Permit2 signatures, setApprovalForAll, EIP-7702 delegation, contract deployment and injected instructions. With an optional wren-guard policy (allowlist, spenders, caps) it also blocks unknown recipients, over-cap amounts and lookalike addresses. It is a static check and stores nothing you send; free demos show real output.
  • wren-guard Pro Paid: one-off digital download, pay what you want at $19, $49 or $99 in USDC on Base (same files at every price); $0.01 sample over x402; the original Python wren-guard is free (MIT)
    wren-guard Pro is a TypeScript guard library for AI agents that hold or move funds on Base and other EVM chains (viem, CDP AgentKit, Privy, Eliza and similar stacks). It enforces allowlisted, capped and simulated sends, decodes calldata and signatures to flag unlimited approvals, Permit, Permit2, setApprovalForAll and EIP-7702 delegation, screens for injected instructions and watches nonces. It ships with an 89-scenario attack corpus drawn from public agent wallet incidents and a GitHub Action that fails CI if your agent's policy would let a known attack through. The original Python wren-guard is free and MIT licensed.
